simple.meaning: מֵחַ (mêach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “fat ; figuratively, rich.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at Psalms 66:15. Its contexts include offering.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֵחַ (H4220).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מֵחַ (mêach) / H4220 is traced through Psalms 66:15, Isaiah 5:17 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4220. meach [ מֵחַ ] noun [masculine] fatling (Phoenician מח fat (adjective ); Late Hebrew מֵיחָא figurative of choice flour ); — only plural absolute: מֵיחִים עֹלוֺת Psa 66:15 burnt offerings of fatlings ; so מֵחִים Isa 5:17 (|| כְּבָשִׂים ) according to Hi Du Che Hpt (read חֳרָבוֺת and strike out גָּרִים ); most, fat ones , figurative for rich men.
